idiom_name: typed Map<string, {resolve, reject}> + AbortSignal.timeout / AsyncLocalStorage context
implementation_notes: TypeScript adds the type discipline this pattern needs rather than new mechanics: a small pending-record interface stored in a Map keyed by the correlation id lets each call be typed to its own reply shape, and the reply router narrows by message id. The runtime work is plain JavaScript - promise, timer, Map - with the deadline as a timer or AbortSignal.timeout(ms) combined through AbortSignal.any for caller-supplied cancellation, and Node's AsyncLocalStorage<CorrelationContext> is how a typed request context (id plus trace fields) is propagated to logs and downstream calls without threading it through every signature. Keeping ids as strings avoids the JSON number-precision trap when the peer is another runtime.
pitfalls: Map<string, Pending<unknown>> erases the reply type, so keep the one unavoidable cast inside a thin typed wrapper per request kind instead of scattering 'as' assertions across call sites.
Timers hold the event loop open: clear them when the reply arrives and call unref() for long deadlines in library code, or a client with no outstanding replies still prevents process exit.

A promise whose entry is deleted without being settled hangs its caller forever, so every removal path - timeout, socket close, validation failure - must reject or the caller leaks a suspended promise.
Correlation ids arriving from the wire are strings (JSON has no 64-bit integer), so never build them as numbers or compare with strict equality against a numeric id.
